name: Plait Solitaire
description: Plait Solitaire (also known as 'Plaits' or 'The Braid') is a double-deck solitaire game of significant complexity and visual appeal. It is distinguished by the 'Plait'â€”a central reserve of 13 cards arranged in a braid-like pattern, where only specific cards are accessible at any time. Requiring the player to manage two sets of foundations and eight tableau piles, it is a game of foresight, sequence planning, and careful reserve management.

overview.description: Plait Solitaire (also known as 'Plaits' or 'The Braid') is a double-deck solitaire game of significant complexity and visual appeal. history.origins: Dates back to the mid-19th century as a complex 'Grand Patience' played in European parlors. The 'Plait' layout was designed to provide a decorative yet difficult reserve element.
timeline: 1865: First appearance in German and British Patience manuals.
1920s: Recorded in 'The Complete Patience' as a benchmark for high-level solo play.
1990s: Implemented in early digital solitaire collections (e.g., BVS Solitaire).
Present: Remains a favorite for players who find Klondike too simple and FreeCell too repetitive.
history.cultural: Often described as the 'Thinking Player's Solitaire' because it rewards memorization of the plait's internal layers.
history.evolution: The game was simplified from even more complex triple-deck versions (like 'The Rope') to maintain a balance between difficulty and table space.

setup.players: One player. Plait is a solo patience game played by a single person; BVS and historical sources describe it as a single-player card game with no opponents or partners.
setup.dealing: Deal 13 cards in a plait (open reserve). Deal 32 cards into 8 tableau piles (4 cards per pile). Place one card above as the first foundation base; the seven other cards of the same rank become foundation bases as they appear. Remainder is stock.

rules.objective: Move all 104 cards to 8 foundation piles, building up in suit from the Base rank (wrapping K to A).
rules.gameplay: Build tableaus down in sequence and alternating color. Only the top card of each tableau pile and the reserve (plait) is available for play on the foundations. One card or a group of cards in proper sequence may move to another tableau pile. When a tableau is empty, any card or legal sequence may fill it. When no moves are available, turn cards from the stock one at a time; cards from stock may move to tableau or foundations. No redeal.
keyRules: Foundations build up in same suit from base rank, wrapping King to Ace.
Tableau builds down in alternating color; only top cards and plait top are available for foundations.
One card or a legal sequence may move to another tableau; empty tableau accepts any card or legal sequence.
Turn stock one card at a time when no other moves; no redeal.

strategy.basic: Free the Plait! The 13 cards in the Plait are your biggest obstacle. Don't use your stock cards or tableau moves if you could instead move a card from the Plait to a foundation. Every card you remove from the Plait increases your tactical options for the rest of the game.
strategy.intermediate: Foundation Focus: Since foundations can start on any rank (like an 8), the sequence is non-standard (8-9-10-J-Q-K-A-2-3-4-5-6-7). Pay close attention to the wrap-around. Don't trap an Ace in a tableau pile unless you have already cleared the Kings for all foundations.
strategy.advanced: The Alternating Trap: While you build down in alternating colors in the tableau, remember that you must eventually build UP in suit in the foundations. If you create a long Black-Red-Black sequence in the tableau, you might be 'Burying' a Diamond and a Heart that are needed for early foundation building. Use empty tableau columns to 'Break' and 'Sort' your suit sequences whenever possible.
tips: Look ahead at the Plait. If the card after the current one is a high-value Base card, prioritize clearing the current card even if it's not ideal for the foundations.
Keep at least one tableau column empty for as long as possibleâ€”it is your most flexible 'Sorting' zone.

variations.name: Standard
variations.description: Standard Plait: 13-card plait reserve, 8 tableau piles (4 cards each), 8 foundations (one base rank revealed at start), remainder stock; build up in suit on foundations, down alternating color on tableau; no redeal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Standard variant uses base game engine; no overrides needed.

variations.name: Similar games
variations.description: Braid, Cadonette and Fort are similar double-deck solitaires documented by BVS but are distinct games with their own rules.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Reference only; these are separate games, not engine variants.
